scenes.text: Imagine driving across a completely flat, barren desert with absolutely nothing in sight for hundreds of miles, where you eventually spot the Tree of Ténéré, once known as the loneliest tree on Earth.
For over a century, this single, beautiful acacia survived in the harsh Sahara by reaching its roots over a hundred feet deep into the dry ground, serving as a sacred landmark for caravan travelers.

But in 1973, the impossible happened when a truck driver, who was reportedly drunk, managed to navigate across miles of empty wasteland only to crash directly into this isolated tree and knock it down.

How is it even mathematically possible to hit the only obstacle in thousands of square miles, and would you blame the driver or just bad luck? Comment your thoughts below and follow for more insane history.
